sentences.gloss: The girl is eating an apple.
The girl is eating the apple.
The teacher is drinking his coffee.
The students are cooking the rice.
The man is drinking a beer.

sentences.text: הוּא אוֹהֵב אֶת הַמָּרָק שֶׁל אִמָּא.

sentences.gloss: Mum is buying salt and sugar.
The pupils want rice and chicken.
The pupil (f.) wants to drink water.
The children don’t want to eat.

sentences.text: אַבָּא לֹא מְבַשֵּׁל אֶת אֲרוּחַת הָעֶרֶב.

sentences.gloss: I (m.) don’t eat any meat at all.

sentences.text: אֲנִי אַף פַּעַם לֹא שׁוֹתֶה קָפֶה.
alts: אֲנִי לֹא שׁוֹתֶה קָפֶה אַף פַּעַם.

sentences.text: הִיא אַף פַּעַם לֹא אוֹכֶלֶת דָּגִים.
alts: הִיא לֹא אוֹכֶלֶת דָּגִים אַף פַּעַם.

sentences.gloss: We have no wine at all.

sentences.text: אֲנִי לֹא רוֹצֶה תֵּה וְלֹא קָפֶה.
sentences.gloss: I (m.) want neither tea nor coffee.

sentences.text: הוּא לֹא אוֹכֵל בָּשָׂר וְלֹא דָּגִים.
sentences.gloss: He eats neither meat nor fish.

sentences.text: אֲנַחְנוּ אַף פַּעַם לֹא קוֹנִים בִּירָה.
alts: אֲנַחְנוּ לֹא קוֹנִים בִּירָה אַף פַּעַם.

sentences.text: אֵין לִי מִיץ וְאֵין לִי מַיִם.
sentences.gloss: I have no juice and no water.

sentences.text: אַף אֶחָד לֹא אוֹכֵל אֶת הַסָּלָט.

sentences.gloss: Do the children want to eat?
Do you (m.) want coffee? — Yes, please.
Do you (f.) want tea? — No, thank you.
Do you (m.) want tea or coffee?
Do you (f.) drink wine or beer?
Do you (pl.) want rice or bread?
Do you (m.) like fruit? — Of course!
Do you (f.) want juice too? — Sure!

sentences.text: יֵשׁ לָךְ חָלָב? לֹא, אֵין לִי.
sentences.gloss: Do you (f.) have milk? — No, I don’t.
